_meta.indication: Treatment of onchocerciasis due to Onchocerca volvulus in patients aged 12 years and older.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled superiority trial with single-dose ivermectin 150 µg/kg as comparator; patients randomized 2:1 to moxidectin or ivermectin.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients aged ≥12 years, weight ≥30 kg, with O. volvulus infection and ≥10 microfilariae/mg skin; recruited from sub-Saharan Africa (DRC, Liberia, Ghana).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: mean O. volvulus skin microfilariae density (mf/mg of skin) at 12 months post-treatment.
pivotal_trials.n: 1472 patients (978 moxidectin, 494 ivermectin received study drug)
pivotal_trials.result: At 12 months, mean skin microfilarial density was 1.79 (moxidectin) vs 9.83 (ivermectin), difference -8.04 (95% CI -9.11, -6.98), p<0.0001; moxidectin was statistically superior.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>10%) were eosinophilia (74% vs 79% ivermectin), pruritus (65% vs 54%), musculoskeletal pain (64% vs 52%), headache (58% vs 54%), and rash (37% vs 21%); most reflect Mazzotti reaction from microfilariae death. Serious/fatal encephalopathy may occur in Loa loa co-infected patients.
target_moa: Anthelmintic active against O. volvulus microfilariae; mechanism not fully known but thought to bind glutamate-gated chloride channels (GluCl), GABA receptors and/or ABC transporters, causing increased permeability, chloride influx, hyperpolarization and muscle paralysis.

advisory_committee.vote: Application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because there were no issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion.

description.text: Broadened indication to include pediatric patients aged 4 to less than 12 years weighing at least 13 kg

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for the broadening of the currently approved indication for moxidectin tablets to include pediatric patients aged 4 to less than 12 years and weighing at least 13 kg.

summary.text: Moxidectin received orphan drug designation for onchocerciasis (September 2010) and was reviewed as a Priority NDA; the sponsor was also granted a tropical disease priority review voucher under section 524 of the FDCA. Approval was based on the pivotal Phase 3 trial (Trial 1) demonstrating superiority over ivermectin in reducing skin microfilariae at 12 months, supported by a Phase 2 dose-ranging trial (Trial 2); it was a first-cycle, traditional approval (not accelerated).

Trial 1 in 1472 patients (NCT 00790998), and Trial 2, a dose-ranging trial (NCT 00300768)
